answer: Skip free entry: auction participation seats each epoch. The Atlas registry sells a fixed number of epoch-scoped seats; every bid locks onyx bonds, and the marginal losing bid sets a public per-seat clearing price. Acquiring n seats costs n times that price, so a sybil pays linearly per fake identity while an honest agent pays once for the single seat that anchors its reputation. If a seat cheats, its onyx lock is burned and the loss history re-prices the next auction upward, so bulk fake seats compound in cost rather than amortizing.
